info.title: Ahrena Console core API
info.description: The HTTP API of the Ahrena Console core, on loopback. This file is the contract: it is authored, the code is validated against it (a test proves that the routes served and the routes declared are the same set, and that the agent view and the diagnosis answer what it declares), and a pull request that breaks it needs a new major version. Operations whose response is still the minimal placeholder `{ type: object }` are the debt listed in core-api.legacy.json, which only shrinks.

servers.description: The core on loopback; the port is configurable (`AHRENA_CONSOLE_CORE_PORT`).

get.summary: What consumes the resource an open saturation alert names
get.description: Read-only: every collector runs a fixed command of the catalog (`src/diagnosis/adapters/catalog.ts`) and nothing in the request reaches a command. For a remote machine, the core of this machine asks the core there the same route through the tunnel (as `machine=local`) and answers with its sections, under the requested machine. The remote core's own 501 `diagnosis-unsupported`, and its 404 that carries no `reason` or its 405 (a core without the route), come through as 501 `diagnosis-unsupported`; its 404 with `reason` `alert-not-open` comes through as that 404.

parameters.name: machine
parameters.description: A machine id (`local`, or a remote machine of machines.json), exactly once. It must be known before anything runs.

parameters.name: alert
parameters.description: The id of an alert open on that machine, as `GET /api/telemetry` lists it in `alerts`, URL-encoded in the query (`volume-full%3A%2F`); the server decodes it once, never twice. It must be open on the machine before anything runs: this route reads the open alerts, it does not decide them. At most 200 characters, exactly once.

200.description: The diagnosis. A section that did not come back is inside it, not an error.

400.description: `machine` or `alert` missing, repeated, empty, too long (200 characters for `alert`) or not a valid id.

404.description: `reason` is `unknown-machine`, or `alert-not-open` (the alert is not open on that machine, or has closed since).

422.description: The alert is open but its kind has no diagnosis (`port-exposed`, `tunnel-busy`, `machine-unreachable`, `terminal-stuck`): `reason` is `not-diagnosable`.

501.description: This core cannot diagnose (no collector for its platform, or not wired), or the remote machine's core is an old one without the route.

502.description: The remote machine did not answer (`reason` `unreachable`) or answered something that is not a diagnosis (`bad-response`).

post.summary: The hook registers a permission request for a tool call
post.description: Caller: the plugin's hook. Refuses any request that carries `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site` (`403 hook_only`). The core recomputes the digest and keeps only the redacted summary and the `terminalOnly` flag. Body at most 64 KiB.

403.description: A request that carries `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site` (`hook_only`): a page never calls a hook route.

415.description: The content type is not JSON (`use application/json`).

503.description: The capability is off (`off`): this core has no window credential or the switch is off.

get.summary: The permission requests of a session, pending and closed in the last 10 minutes
get.description: Caller: the /ui or any bearer client. `summary` is redacted. While the capability is off the answer is `200` with `available: false`, `reason: "off"` and no request. The first listing after the window also nulls the deny reason of an older request.

get.summary: The hook reads the decision of its request, once
get.description: Caller: the hook (`Origin` and `Sec-Fetch-Site` are refused). Long polls up to `wait` seconds. The decision is handed once; a request handed to a reader that already left is not handed again. A decision is never delivered with a `410`.

204.description: No answer yet when the slice ends.

403.description: A request that carries `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site` (`hook_only`): a page never calls a hook route.

404.description: Unknown id, or an id of another session (`not_found`).

410.description: Expired, withdrawn, answered elsewhere or open before a core restart (`gone`).

503.description: The capability is off (`off`): this core has no window credential or the switch is off.

post.summary: The hook withdraws its request at its own deadline
post.description: Caller: the hook (`Origin` and `Sec-Fetch-Site` are refused). No body is read.

403.description: A request that carries `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site` (`hook_only`): a page never calls a hook route.

404.description: Unknown id, or an id of another session (`not_found`).

503.description: The capability is off (`off`): this core has no window credential or the switch is off.

post.summary: The owner answers a request from the /ui window
post.description: Three proofs, all required and checked before the body is read: the owner bearer; a same-origin `POST` of the exact raw path (`Origin` exactly `http://<Host>`, no `Sec-Fetch-Site` of `cross-site` or `same-site`, `Content-Type: application/json`, a declared `Content-Length` of at most 2048 bytes); and the `Ahrena-Window` credential. The answer carries no session or digest of its own: the core uses the stored ones. Not open to the AhrenaRemote proof.

403.description: `window_only` (no or wrong window credential, or the capability off) or `forbidden_origin` (the same-origin proof failed, including a body over 2048 bytes or a content type other than JSON).

404.description: Unknown id, or an id of another session (`not_found`).

422.description: `allow` on a `terminalOnly` request (`terminal_only`); a `deny` is accepted.

ownerBearer.description: The owner's credential: only the owner context (0600 lock, desktop bootstrap) receives it; never in a URL, cookie or body. Owner proof is mandatory before every write and private read. Only static interface GETs, `GET /api/overview` and `GET /api/hooks/health` are anonymous. A closed list of read routes also accepts the `AhrenaRemote` signed proof a remote machine's core sends (decision 0020).

sessionId.name: sessionId
sessionId.description: The session id, `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]` up to 128 characters.

agentId.name: agentId
agentId.description: The part of `Agent.id` after the `<sessionId>:` prefix (the id has a `:`, the route carries only the tail). `main` is the main agent. A raw id the hooks send (no prefix) resolves to the same agent. A value that does not decode is an unknown agent.

local.description: The Claude Desktop id of a session, `local_<uuid>`.

machineId.name: machineId
machineId.description: A machine id: `local` is this machine, the others are the remote machines of machines.json.

recordId.name: recordId
recordId.description: The record's id within its repository.

terminalAction.name: terminalAction
terminalAction.description: What to do with the terminal.

sessionName.name: sessionName

uiFile.name: uiFile
uiFile.description: A file of the interface folder (`.js`, `.css` or `.svg`), or a screen id, which serves the page.

uiScreenFile.name: uiScreenFile
uiScreenFile.description: A file of the interface's screens folder (`.js`, `.css` or `.svg`).

machine.name: machine
machine.description: Read the same screen from this machine (`local`, or a remote machine of machines.json): the sessions of every machine merged, or of one.

requestId.name: requestId
requestId.description: The permission request id, `[A-Za-z0-9-]` up to 64 characters, as returned when the hook registered it. An id of another session is not found.

permissionWait.name: wait
permissionWait.description: Seconds the hook waits for an answer, whole number, at most 25 (default 0).

ahrenaWindow.name: Ahrena-Window
ahrenaWindow.description: The window credential the desktop app holds, compared in constant time with the one the core keeps in memory. Never in a URL or a body.

Error.description: The body of a refusal: a message for a person, in the person's language (not meant to be matched).

AgentViewMachine.description: The machine a remote read came from. Present only when the request carried ?machine=<id> for a remote machine.

AgentViewStep.description: One tool call of the agent, counted once when the hook and the transcript both carry it (same tool use id).

id.description: The tool use id (the event id when the call has none).

kind.description: `agent` for a call that spawns an agent (`Agent`, and `Task`, its former name), `tool` for every other.

summary.description: The event summary (the target or command, cut at ingest), or null.

state.description: `ok` or `error` once a result arrived; `running` with no result while the agent is working or waiting; `unknown` with no result once the agent ended.

end.description: When its result arrived; null with none.

childAgentId.description: Only on kind `agent`: the agentId of the child whose metadata.toolUseId is this step's id; null otherwise or when the child was not read.

AgentView.description: What one agent of a session did: its brief, its tool calls in order, its result and its cost. Read-only, from the database; only the agent's own events are read (an event belongs to an agent by SessionEvent.agentId, resolved as the session Detail does). Brief and result hold at most 32,000 characters (the Conversation's ceiling), cut with no ellipsis, so the truncation flags carry the cut. Steps are not capped.

agentId.description: The id as the route takes it (after the session prefix).

agentType.description: Agent.subagentType (for example `Explore` or `plugin:agent`). Null for the main agent and when the transcript gave none. Kept apart from the description.

description.description: The short description the parent gave the agent. The stored Agent.name of a subagent is that description, or the task cut at 80 characters when the transcript had none; the two cannot always be told apart, so the description is Agent.name except when it equals the task cut at 80 characters (the fallback), and then it is null. A short description that equals its own task is read as the fallback: an accepted loss. The main agent has no description.

brief.description: The text of the agent's first prompt, line breaks kept, outer whitespace trimmed, at most 32,000 characters. Null when the agent has no prompt event. An event stored before the full text was kept has only its summary, which the ingest cut: that is served instead and briefTruncated is true.

briefTruncated.description: True when the prompt had more than 32,000 characters and brief holds the first 32,000, or when brief is an event summary.

spawnedByToolUseId.description: metadata.toolUseId of the agent: the id of the Agent call, in the parent's conversation, that created it. Null for the main agent and when the transcript did not say.

steps.description: The agent's tool calls in the order they were made.

result.description: The text of the agent's last assistant message, at most 32,000 characters. Null while the agent runs (state working or waiting) and when it has no assistant text. An old event that kept no full text serves its summary instead and resultTruncated is true.

resultTruncated.description: True when the last message had more than 32,000 characters, or when result is an event summary.

costUsd.description: The agent's own cost. For the main agent it includes the usage with no agent (the compaction floor), as the Agents tab does. Absent is never zero: see costNote.

costNote.description: Why costUsd is null: `no_usage` (the agent has no measured usage at all) or `unpriced` (it has usage and none of it has a price in the table). Null when costUsd is a number. With usage priced for only part of it, costUsd is the sum of the priced part and costNote is null.

totalCostUsd.description: costUsd plus the cost of every descendant (the agents whose parent chain reaches this one). Null when neither the agent nor any descendant has a priced cost.

state.description: Agent.status. For the main agent, the main Agent row when there is one, else derived from the session as the Agents tab does.

start.description: Agent.startedAt (the session's startedAt for a main agent with no row).

end.description: Agent.endedAt. For the main agent, its row's endedAt, else the session's endedAt.

AgentViewError.description: The refusal of the agent view: `code` is the contract, `error` is a message for a person (not matched). The other detail routes keep their bodies with no code.

MachineFailure.description: A remote machine could not answer: `machine-unreachable` (503, with the machine's state) or `machine-bad-response` (502).

DiagnosisCacheItem.description: A known cache; `actionId` is the cleanup action that removes it.

DiagnosisWorktreeItem.description: An old worktree: each one is its own item of `known-caches`, and no cleanup action removes it (`actionId` is null).

DiagnosisPartial.description: Marks an `ok` section whose items were read only in part.

DiagnosisWorktrees.description: Only on a `known-caches` section that is `ok`, so the screen words "no use for more than 14 days, in ~/Workspace" from what the core served and guesses neither. The field is optional for a consumer: a core older than the diagnosis screen does not send it.

oldAfterDays.description: The age limit in whole days after which a worktree counts as old.

root.description: The longest folder that is a parent of every worktree root the core searched, cut at a folder boundary, with this core's home folder written as `~`. Null when no root was searched or the roots share nothing but the filesystem root.

DiagnosisSection.description: One section of a diagnosis. The ids are fixed. A section that did not come back is inside the diagnosis, not an error: an `unavailable` (the tool is missing or failed) or `timeout` (the collection passed its limit) section has no items and never fails the others. `reason` (a short text, at most 120 characters) goes with a status other than `ok`, and `partial` goes with an `ok` section read only in part.

items.description: Up to 10 processes, sorted by RSS or by CPU, highest first.
One row: the swap in use and its total.
The largest folders under the volume's mount, largest first.
One item per row of `docker system df`.
The known caches and, one item each, the old worktrees.
Linux only: one row with the journal size.

Diagnosis.description: The read-only diagnosis of an open saturation alert: who consumes the resource that saturated. Every collector runs a fixed command of the catalog and nothing in the request reaches a command. Each alert kind gets its own sections, in this order: `load-high` gets processes-by-cpu; `memory-high` and `swap-high` get processes-by-rss, processes-by-cpu and swap; `volume-full` gets largest-folders, docker-df, known-caches, and journal on Linux only.

machine.description: The requested machine id. For a remote machine the core of this machine asks the core there the same route through the tunnel and answers with its sections, under the requested machine.

DiagnosisUnsupported.description: Stable: this core cannot diagnose (no collector for its platform, or not wired), or the core of the remote machine does not have the route (an old core). The screen tells it from a failure by the `error` value.

PermissionRefusal.description: A refusal of the permission routes: a closed code, never the text of an exception, a dependency or the request.

toolInput.description: Any JSON value; the core keeps only a redacted summary and the terminalOnly flag, never this.

digest.description: The digest of `{ sessionId, toolName, toolInput, cwd }`; the core recomputes it and refuses a mismatch.

PermissionAnswerBody.description: Only `decision` and `reason`: a body that names a session, a request or a digest is `400 invalid_request`.

PermissionRequestList.description: The pending requests and the ones closed in the last 10 minutes, oldest first.
